newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet/diesel spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet/diesel spread narrows.

text.p: The jet fuel/gas oil spread was poised to slip to negative levels as the recent narrowing in values between the two products continued, traders said Thursday.

This is because gas oil values remained strong, while jet continued to trade lower. A Singapore trader bought a total of 400,000 barrels of jet fuel in four cargoes from two European majors on Thursday.
Two cargoes were bought at $27.30 a barrel for March 28-April 1 lifting fob, and another two were purchased at $26.70 for April 6-11.
On Wednesday, the same trader bought two cargoes at $28.70 amd $27.50 for end-March and early April respectively.

Traders said the spread has narrowed for physical end March cargoes and has even gone into negative levels for early April cargoes. Swaps regrade for March slipped to be offered at 70 cents a barrel, from $1.00 on Wednesday, and April at 25/40 cents, from 50/70 cents.
The Singapore trader might soon cease its jet fuel purchases judging from the lower prices it were willing to pay, trade sources said.
But its gas oil purchases could continue for some time, they said.

On Thursday, the trader bought 150,000 barrels from the European major at $27.10 for April 6-11 lifting fob. The trader had also bid for another early April cargo to as high as $28.10 a barrel but there were no offers.
The trader has bought as much as 2.32 million barrels over two weeks.
But some traders said the market would not be able to sustain the current high levels once the Singapore trader completed his purchases.
They see the support at $25.00 a barrel which was the level seen during end February.
